# Five Locks Escape

A Skill Harbor house build: an escape game of five locks in a chain, refereed by your own Muse. Pick a theme, and your assistant generates all five puzzles in one pass, before the game starts. Each solved puzzle hands you the word, code, or key the next lock actually needs: the solution of lock one is the decryption key, the reading order, or the selection word of lock two, and so on to the fifth door. It is a real chain, not five unrelated riddles in the same decor, and the difficulty rises along the way.

The refereeing is the anti-cheating design. Before the first puzzle is shown, the complete answer key is written into a sealed game state file: every solution, every accepted spelling variant, every hint text, every chain link. Nothing is invented mid-game and nothing leaks early: you only ever see one lock at a time. Your proposals get the same neutral verdict, correct or incorrect, never a warm or cold hint, and an answer counts only if it matches the key as written, after a fair normalization of case, accents, and separators. You share 3 hints for the whole game, one per lock at most, each costing 5 points. Scoring is plain: 20 points per lock solved, 100 for a perfect run, minus the hints you spent. And no lock can trap you forever: after enough failed attempts the referee offers to force the lock, it opens for 0 points, and the piece of the chain hidden inside it is handed over as a mechanism so the next lock stays playable.
